\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{संकट} (saṅkaṭ)}{संकट (saṅkaṭ)}]{\hi{संकट} (saṅkaṭ) — a crisis}

\label{lesson:HI-C383-sankat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to rub hard, then the Hindi for fragile.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{संकट}}
\textbf{\hi{संकट}} — \emph{saṅkaṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a crisis\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{बारिश} \hi{नहीं} \hi{होगी} \hi{तो} \hi{किसानों} \hi{पर} \hi{संकट} \hi{आएगा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bāriś nahīṃ hogī to kisānoṁ par saṅkaṭ āegā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it doesn't rain, the farmers will face a crisis.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{संकट}} (\emph{saṅkaṭ}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{saṃkaṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}narrow; dangerous, critical\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṅkaṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṅkaṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar bāriś nahīṃ hogī to kisānoṁ par saṅkaṭ āegā.} — If it doesn't rain, the farmers will face a crisis.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to rub hard, then the Hindi for fragile, then say \emph{saṅkaṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{संकट} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A crisis\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{हानि} (hāni)}{हानि (hāni)}]{\hi{हानि} (hāni) — damage, harm (formal)}

\label{lesson:HI-C383-hani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for fragile, then the Hindi for a crisis.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{हानि}}
\textbf{\hi{हानि}} — \emph{hāni} — \textquotedblleft{}damage, harm (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{तुम} \hi{रात} \hi{भर} \hi{जागोगे} \hi{तो} \hi{सेहत} \hi{को} \hi{हानि} \hi{होगी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum rāt bhar jāgoge to sehat ko hāni hogī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you stay up all night, your health will suffer.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{हानि}} (\emph{hāni}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{hāni}, \textquotedblleft{}giving up; loss\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hāni}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum rāt bhar jāgoge to sehat ko hāni hogī.} — If you stay up all night, your health will suffer.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for fragile, then the Hindi for a crisis, then say \emph{hāni} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{घातक} (ghātak)}{घातक (ghātak)}]{\hi{घातक} (ghātak) — deadly, fatal}

\label{lesson:HI-C383-ghatak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a crisis, then the Hindi for damage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{घातक}}
\textbf{\hi{घातक}} — \emph{ghātak} — \textquotedblleft{}deadly, fatal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{इलाज} \hi{नहीं} \hi{होगा} \hi{तो} \hi{यह} \hi{बीमारी} \hi{घातक} \hi{हो} \hi{सकती} \hi{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ilāj nahīṃ hogā to yah bīmārī ghātak ho saktī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Without treatment this illness can be fatal.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{घातक}} (\emph{ghātak}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{ghātaka}, \textquotedblleft{}killing, destructive\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghātak}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar ilāj nahīṃ hogā to yah bīmārī ghātak ho saktī hai.} — Without treatment this illness can be fatal.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a crisis, then the Hindi for damage, then say \emph{ghātak} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{उधेड़ना} (udheṛnā)}{उधेड़ना (udheṛnā)}]{\hi{उधेड़ना} (udheṛnā) — to unpick, to unravel}

\label{lesson:HI-C383-udherna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for damage, then the Hindi for deadly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{उधेड़ना}}
\textbf{\hi{उधेड़ना}} — \emph{udheṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to unpick, to unravel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{तुम} \hi{यह} \hi{धागा} \hi{खींचोगे} \hi{तो} \hi{पूरा} \hi{स्वेटर} \hi{उधेड़} \hi{दोगे।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum yah dhāgā khīñcoge to pūrā sveṭar udheṛ doge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you pull this thread, you'll unravel the whole jumper.
\end{quote}

Past, with \hi{ने} (he or she …): \hi{उसने} \hi{पुराना} \hi{स्वेटर} \hi{उधेड़ा}, \emph{usne purānā sveṭar udheṛā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{उधेड़ना}} (\emph{udheṛnā}) is a tadbhava, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{uddharati}, \textquotedblleft{}takes out\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2009).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udheṛnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udheṛnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum yah dhāgā khīñcoge to pūrā sveṭar udheṛ doge.} — If you pull this thread, you'll unravel the whole jumper.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for damage, then the Hindi for deadly, then say \emph{udheṛnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{भीगना} (bhīgnā)}{भीगना (bhīgnā)}]{\hi{भीगना} (bhīgnā) — to get wet, to get soaked}

\label{lesson:HI-C383-bhigna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for deadly, then the Hindi for to unravel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{भीगना}}
\textbf{\hi{भीगना}} — \emph{bhīgnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to get wet, to get soaked\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{छाता} \hi{ले} \hi{लो}, \hi{वरना} \hi{भीग} \hi{जाओगे।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chātā le lo, varnā bhīg jāoge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Take an umbrella, or you'll get soaked.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \hi{वह} \hi{बारिश} \hi{में} \hi{भीग} \hi{गया}, \emph{vah bāriś meṁ bhīg gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{भीगना}} (\emph{bhīgnā}) is inherited from \emph{*bhiyagna}, \textquotedblleft{}smeared, wet\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 9500).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhīgnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chātā le lo, varnā bhīg jāoge.} — Take an umbrella, or you'll get soaked.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for deadly, then the Hindi for to unravel, then say \emph{bhīgnā} again
\end{itemize}
